name: Reading and Replicating ML Papers
strandNote: Optional on every quant track. For AI research roles and for research desks that read machine learning papers.
description: Read a machine learning paper for its claim and evidence, replicate one result on a laptop, and write an honest note on what held.

levels.name: How to read an ML paper

requires.why: Reads scaling-law plots and the Chinchilla paper, met in gpt level 4.
Uses the reading order and the tolerance rule from the momentum paper; a check, since its prerequisites are long.
Reuses the toy model of superposition trained in interp level 3 for a second figure of the paper.
Builds on seeds, ablations and the paired comparison across seeds from nn-train level 4.
Builds on standard errors, contamination checks and judge bias from post-train level 4.
Applies the corrections for many tests from testing level 3 to many benchmarks.

lessonObjectives.l1-the-claim: Turn an abstract into one testable claim with a number, a comparison and a condition.
lessonObjectives.l2-baselines: Judge whether a baseline had the same data, compute and tuning as the method it is compared with.
lessonObjectives.l3-ablations: Read an ablation table and say which component carries the gain and which effects interact.
lessonObjectives.l4-plots-on-log-axes: Derive a slope and a fitted exponent from points read off a log-log plot.
lessonObjectives.l5-a-replication-target: Choose one result to replicate, with a tolerance, a compute budget and a stopping rule.
lessonObjectives.l6-the-phase-diagram: Replicate the two-feature phase diagram of the toy-models paper and compare it with the figure.
lessonObjectives.l7-fitting-a-scaling-law: Implement the fit of Chinchilla's third approach with a Huber loss and many starts.
lessonObjectives.l8-when-it-does-not-match: Diagnose a replication gap: rounding, fitting choices, missing details or a wrong claim.
lessonObjectives.l9-seeds-and-spread: Measure the spread of a result across seeds and say how many seeds a claim needs.
lessonObjectives.l10-error-bars-that-mean-something: Build a paired confidence interval for a difference, over seeds and over evaluation items.
lessonObjectives.l11-threats-to-validity: List the threats to a result's validity, from contamination to tuning on the test set.
lessonObjectives.l12-the-replication-note: Write a replication note that states what matched, what did not and what was not tried.
